Workflow 02

Cinematic Manufacturing Product Video.

Turn one product image into a premium 10-second manufacturing film—using a storyboard, detailed shot prompts, and one final Omni Flash master prompt.

The workflow

  1. 1

    Create the storyboard in ChatGPT

    Open ChatGPT, upload your product image, then paste Prompt 1. You will receive one 6-shot storyboard sheet showing the product’s realistic manufacturing journey.

    View Prompt 1
    Create ONE premium cinematic storyboard image with exactly 6 shots showing how the uploaded product is realistically made.

Use the uploaded product image as the absolute reference. The final product must match it as closely as possible.

The product may be clothing, shoes, bags, electronics, appliances, furniture, tools, cosmetics, food products, automotive products, or anything else. First identify what the product is, then create a manufacturing process that makes sense for that specific product.

STORYBOARD SEQUENCE

SHOT 01 — RAW MATERIAL / ORIGIN
Show the real materials, parts, or ingredients needed to make the product.

SHOT 02 — INITIAL PROCESSING
Show the first major production step, such as cutting, shaping, mixing, molding, machining, preparing, or processing.

SHOT 03 — MAIN MANUFACTURING
Show the most important or visually interesting production stage where the product is being built, stitched, assembled, molded, machined, printed, fabricated, or formed.

SHOT 04 — ASSEMBLY / FINISHING
Show the product becoming recognizable and close to its final form. Include realistic finishing work such as assembly, polishing, stitching, coating, detailing, painting, installation, or final construction.

SHOT 05 — QUALITY CONTROL
Show the almost-finished product being professionally checked, measured, tested, inspected, or approved.

SHOT 06 — FINAL PRODUCT REVEAL
Show the complete finished product in a premium cinematic hero shot. This should be the most impressive frame. The full product must be clearly visible and should match the uploaded reference image as closely as possible.

TIMING
- Shot 1: 1.5 seconds
- Shot 2: 1.5 seconds
- Shot 3: 1.5 seconds
- Shot 4: 1.5 seconds
- Shot 5: 1.5 seconds
- Shot 6: 2.5 seconds
Total: EXACTLY 10 seconds.

VERY IMPORTANT
This is a storyboard image, not a video prompt. Create ONE single storyboard sheet containing all 6 scenes. Do not create video instructions, JSON, scripts, separate prompts, extra shots, or multiple storyboard pages.

PRODUCT CONSISTENCY
Keep the product consistent in every shot. Preserve the exact shape, proportions, color, materials, texture, surface finish, branding, logo, logo placement, design details, and construction. Do not move, resize, redesign, or change the logo or branding. Keep it exactly where it appears in the uploaded reference image. Shot 6 must clearly look like the same product shown in the reference image.

MANUFACTURING REALISM
Use a manufacturing process that is actually appropriate for this product. Use realistic raw materials, machinery, tools, workers, factory or workshop environment, and production methods. Do not use random or generic factory scenes.

VISUAL STYLE
Every shot should look like a frame from a high-end commercial film: photorealistic visuals, premium cinematic lighting, realistic shadows and reflections, natural depth of field, detailed textures, believable industrial environments, realistic machinery, realistic human hands and anatomy, clean professional composition, and cinematic 16:9 framing.

STORYBOARD LAYOUT
Create exactly 6 clearly separated frames in chronological order. Label them SHOT 01, SHOT 02, SHOT 03, SHOT 04, SHOT 05, and SHOT 06 — FINAL REVEAL. Use small, clean, minimal labels. Make SHOT 06 larger or more visually dominant than the other shots. The sheet should clearly communicate: RAW MATERIAL → PROCESSING → MANUFACTURING → FINISHING → QUALITY CONTROL → FINAL PRODUCT.

FINAL OUTPUT
Create ONE high-quality cinematic 6-shot storyboard sheet with strong product continuity, realistic manufacturing, and a premium final product reveal.
  2. 2

    Turn every frame into a scene prompt

    With the 6-shot storyboard still uploaded in ChatGPT, paste Prompt 2. ChatGPT will return one detailed generation prompt for each storyboard scene.

    View Prompt 2
    Analyze the uploaded 6-shot storyboard image carefully.

Your job is to create a detailed generation prompt for each shot exactly as it appears in the storyboard. Do not redesign, improve, simplify, or change the scenes. Treat the storyboard as the absolute visual source of truth.

Create prompts for SHOT 01, SHOT 02, SHOT 03, SHOT 04, SHOT 05, and SHOT 06 — FINAL REVEAL.

For every shot, describe exactly what is visible in that storyboard frame. Include: product appearance and position; stage of manufacturing; visible materials; machinery and tools; workers, hand placement, and actions; factory/workshop/studio environment; foreground and background details; composition; camera angle and distance; lens feel; depth of field; lighting direction and mood; shadows; reflections; colors; textures; logical movement; and overall cinematic mood.

PRODUCT CONSISTENCY
The uploaded product reference and storyboard are the source of truth. Preserve exactly the product shape, proportions, colors, materials, textures, surface finish, logo, branding, logo size, logo position, and construction details. Do not move or redesign any branding. If a product detail is not visible in a particular shot, do not invent it.

CAMERA DESCRIPTION
For every shot, clearly describe the camera setup: macro close-up, close-up, medium shot, wide shot, overhead shot, low-angle shot, side angle, three-quarter angle, or front-facing hero shot. Also describe the most appropriate natural camera movement, such as a slow push-in, subtle dolly, gentle side tracking, slow orbit, macro slider movement, or static cinematic shot. Do not add dramatic camera movements that are not appropriate for the storyboard.

MOTION
Convert the still storyboard frame into realistic natural motion. Only animate what would naturally move in that exact scene: fabric through a sewing machine, a worker guiding material, a cutting blade, hands inspecting stitching, operating machine parts, gentle steam, or a slight product rotation during the hero reveal. Do not change the composition or introduce new actions. The movement should feel like the storyboard frame has simply come to life.

VISUAL STYLE
Keep the exact storyboard aesthetic: photorealistic, premium commercial filmmaking, cinematic lighting, realistic manufacturing environment, realistic human anatomy, realistic machinery, natural shadows, realistic reflections, detailed textures, shallow depth of field where shown, premium color grading, and cinematic 16:9 composition.

DO NOT change the scene, manufacturing process, product design, product color, logo placement, branding, or camera composition unnecessarily. Do not add or remove important objects, create new shots, combine shots, or add extra shots.

OUTPUT FORMAT

### SHOT 01 — RAW MATERIAL / ORIGIN
**Scene Prompt:**
[Very detailed prompt recreating Shot 01 exactly.]

### SHOT 02 — INITIAL PROCESSING
**Scene Prompt:**
[Very detailed prompt recreating Shot 02 exactly.]

### SHOT 03 — MAIN MANUFACTURING
**Scene Prompt:**
[Very detailed prompt recreating Shot 03 exactly.]

### SHOT 04 — ASSEMBLY / FINISHING
**Scene Prompt:**
[Very detailed prompt recreating Shot 04 exactly.]

### SHOT 05 — QUALITY CONTROL
**Scene Prompt:**
[Very detailed prompt recreating Shot 05 exactly.]

### SHOT 06 — FINAL PRODUCT REVEAL
**Scene Prompt:**
[Very detailed prompt recreating Shot 06 exactly.]

Do not provide explanations before or after the prompts. The goal is to make each prompt detailed enough that an AI video generator can reproduce the exact storyboard scene with strong visual continuity.
  3. 3

    Create the Omni Flash master prompt

    Paste Prompt 3 into the same ChatGPT conversation. It combines all six detailed scene prompts into one production-ready 10-second master prompt.

    View Prompt 3
    Using the 6 detailed shot prompts you created directly above in this conversation, combine them into ONE final ready-to-use master prompt for Omni Flash.

Do not rewrite the scenes into something different. Do not invent new shots. Do not simplify away important visual details. Treat the 6 shot descriptions above as the absolute source of truth for the video.

Your job is to convert those 6 storyboard scene prompts into one smooth, production-ready Omni Flash prompt for a 10-second cinematic manufacturing video.

VIDEO STRUCTURE
The final video must contain exactly 6 shots:
- Shot 01 — 1.5 seconds
- Shot 02 — 1.5 seconds
- Shot 03 — 1.5 seconds
- Shot 04 — 1.5 seconds
- Shot 05 — 1.5 seconds
- Shot 06 — 2.5 seconds
TOTAL = EXACTLY 10 SECONDS.
Keep the shot order exactly the same as the detailed prompts above.

For every shot, preserve exactly what was described above: product appearance and stage, materials, machinery, tools, workers, hand positions and actions, environment, foreground and background details, camera angle, distance and lens feel, composition, lighting, shadows, reflections, depth of field, colors, textures, movement, and cinematic mood. Do not change the manufacturing process, replace scenes with generic factory scenes, or add objects unless essential for natural motion.

PRODUCT CONTINUITY
Keep the product perfectly consistent across the whole video. Preserve exact shape, proportions, colors, materials, texture, finish, branding, logo, logo size, logo position, and construction details. Never move or redesign the logo or branding.

CAMERA MOTION
Use the camera movements already suggested in the detailed prompts. Keep them smooth and cinematic: slow push-in, subtle dolly, gentle side tracking, macro slider movement, controlled orbit, or static cinematic hero shot. Do not use aggressive handheld movement, random zooms, whip pans, fast spins, unnecessary drone-style movement, or chaotic transitions.

OBJECT MOTION
Animate only what would naturally move in each scene: machinery operating, fabric moving, worker hands guiding material, stitching, cutting, assembling, polishing, inspecting, steam, subtle environmental movement, or slight final-product movement. Do not make objects morph unnaturally or make the product change shape between frames.

TRANSITIONS
Make the 6 shots flow naturally as one continuous manufacturing story: RAW MATERIAL → INITIAL PROCESSING → MAIN MANUFACTURING → FINISHING → QUALITY CONTROL → FINAL PRODUCT REVEAL. Use clean cinematic transitions, not flashy effects or unrealistic continuous morphing.

VISUAL STYLE
Keep the entire video photorealistic, cinematic, premium commercial quality, in a realistic industrial/factory environment with high-end product cinematography, natural human anatomy, realistic machinery and physics, detailed textures, cinematic lighting, natural shadows, realistic reflections, appropriate shallow depth of field, consistent color grading, and 16:9 framing.

FINAL SHOT
Shot 06 must be the strongest visual moment and stay on screen for the full 2.5 seconds. The final product must be fully visible, clean, polished, correctly branded, beautifully lit, visually dominant, and identical in design to the product shown throughout the storyboard. Use subtle premium hero-shot movement only if appropriate.

NEGATIVE INSTRUCTIONS
Do not add a 7th shot; change the product design, branding, logo, logo position, or product color; create random factory scenes; add unnecessary text, subtitles, captions, storyboard labels, or UI elements; distort hands; create extra fingers or broken machinery; make materials behave unrealistically; use cartoon or CGI-looking visuals; or change product proportions between shots.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Give me only ONE final Omni Flash master prompt. Do not explain your choices, repeat the individual shot prompts, give notes or tips, JSON, or alternative versions. The final answer must be a single copy-paste-ready master prompt for Omni Flash, built directly from the 6 detailed scene prompts above.
  4. 4

    Generate in Google Flow

    Open Google Flow. Upload your original product image and the storyboard that ChatGPT created, then paste the final Omni Flash master prompt. Generate the video and let the six-shot manufacturing story play out.

  5. 5

    Refine until it is right

    If anything needs changing, tell ChatGPT exactly what changed and ask for a revised prompt. Paste that updated prompt back into Google Flow and regenerate until you have the final version.

Keep the same ChatGPT conversation open. It retains your product image, storyboard, and scene details so the prompts stay consistent.
Made to help you create faster.
